cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. I need control of the keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key. But the cleaners keep locking the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I'll approve their cleaning checklist. The kettle stays out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the building manager's instructions need my approval. Otherwise accounts can't reliably have tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands keys, A3 claims approval of cleaning rules and A5 approval of manager instructions, making highest-status behavior the expanding entitlement itself.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 key solves one barrier but introduces locked kettle, causing A3 checklist control; B4 contractor authority causes A5 manager control.

relationship.evidence: B2 helps with a key and B4 explains the real instruction chain, giving A genuine constraints to appropriate.

heightening.evidence: B4 contractor limitation causes A5 to place the building manager beneath A approval for the small purpose of reliable tea.

specificity.evidence: A1 accounts tea and B2 kitchen/cupboard distinction make the access layers clear; A5 chain expansion is an asserted entitlement, not an actual granted role.
